copy.blurb:
The model fancies Japan more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against Sweden. +14.3pp is a wide disagreement by the engine's standards; that's what fires this as a Pick on the home side.

Public Elo rates Japan 130 points higher than the other side (Japan 1790, Sweden 1660). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Japan to win at 53%, the draw at 22%, and Sweden to win at 25%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Japan on the win side reads 53%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Japan to win at 38%, the draw at 24%, and Sweden to win at 28%. Polymarket has Japan at 38%, which prices out at American odds of +160; the model has the same side at 53%. The +14.3pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Japan side that lower bound is 43% — +4.3pp clear of the market's 38%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Japan priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 34 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: This is a selection call on the Japan side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Japan side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Japan look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 53% vs market 38% — a +14.3pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: Japan v Sweden · the model leans Japan
